newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wheat quality disappoints in Germany's north.
newsitem.headline: Wheat quality disappoints in Germany's north.

text.p: Late harvesting efforts in the northern German states of Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt produced large wheat volumes of disappointing qualities, the grain trade paper Ernaehrungsdienst (ED) wrote.
Traders believed high nominal prices may have to ease amid competition from France in both domestic and third country markets, it said.

Protein contents in Lower Saxony varied between nine and 16 percent while wheat yields in the key agricultural state should vary between 6.0 and 12 tonnes per hectare compared with last year's national wheat average of 6.9 tph.
Breadwheat needs 12.5 percent, with premiums paid for 13 and 14.

Hagberg falling numbers between 250 and 380 were satsifactory but this was offset by the protein problems and the fact that some 60 percent of the wheat harvested was of "B" quality, which describes lower baking qualities than those found in "A" and top "E" grades.
In Saxony-Anhalt, Lower Saxony's eastern neighbrour, some 25-30 percent of the wheat crop reportedly failed to show adequate falling numbers.
But 48 percent of the crop were estimated to be of "E" quality, followed by 30 percent of "A" grades.
ED said French sellers prices of 287.50 marks a tonne cif Benelux were competitive, with German wheat still nominally above 300. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
